title: Bakery commissions sharing a glaze supplier

threads.title: Orchard Hall wedding cake
threads.scope: Design, bake, deliver and review the citrus wedding cake commissioned for the October Orchard Hall wedding.

threads.title: Stone Pier cafe launch pastries
threads.scope: Develop and supply pastries for the separately commissioned Stone Pier cafe opening.

threads.title: Aquarium filter replacement
threads.scope: Replace a noisy filter in a home aquarium.

captures.text: Orchard Hall October wedding order: three-tier citrus cake, pale green glaze, delivery before the ceremony. Tasting included in this commission.
captures.rationale: The order defines one cake commission including development and delivery.

captures.text: Stone Pier cafe hired us for opening-day pastries under a separate order. They want the same pale green glaze but individual pear cakes.
captures.rationale: A distinct client event and deliverable establish another commission.

captures.text: Supplier slip OCR: Meadow Glazes, pale green, batch 17, two tubs. My job-reference line is cropped out of the photo.
captures.rationale: The common supplier and color do not identify which commission received the tubs.

captures.text: Orchard Hall tasting: citrus sponge approved. Keep the bottom tier less sweet so the glaze does not dominate.
captures.rationale: Tasting refines the already commissioned wedding cake.

captures.text: Aquarium clip: filter rattles even after cleaning the impeller. Replacement housing should fit behind the tank lid.
captures.rationale: Home aquarium maintenance is unrelated to the bakery orders.

captures.text: Found the uncropped Meadow Glazes slip: one tub was allocated to the Orchard Hall wedding cake and one to the Stone Pier opening pastries.
captures.rationale: The allocation explicitly establishes a shared receipt spanning both projects.

captures.text: Stone Pier opening trial: pear cakes held their shape for four hours. Increase the pastry count from 60 to 72 for the opening order.
captures.rationale: Testing and quantity planning continue the cafe-opening commission.

captures.text: Orchard Hall cake assembly checklist: chill all three tiers, fit the support dowels, and reserve the labeled wedding glaze tub.
captures.rationale: Assembly executes the wedding cake design.

captures.text: The Orchard Hall wedding cake reached the venue upright. Photograph the final table placement before returning the transport box.
captures.rationale: Delivery remains within the cake commission.

captures.text: Stone Pier opening-day counter photo: the 72 pear cakes are on trays beside the cafe's launch sign; the delivery docket is signed.
captures.rationale: Documents completion of the separate cafe supply order.

captures.text: Wedding cake feedback from Orchard Hall: citrus balance praised; one glaze edge scuffed during table placement. Add a wider carry board to this job's review.
captures.rationale: Client feedback and lessons close the wedding commission.

captures.text: Meadow Glazes reconciliation: charge one batch-17 tub to Orchard Hall wedding and one to Stone Pier opening; neither client should receive the other's delivery fee.
captures.rationale: A shared accounting source spans both jobs while preserving their separation.

events.reason: The uncropped allocation in c06 confirms that the receipt serves both orders. Link the supplier slip to both without merging the commissions.

events.text: Supplier slip OCR corrected: Meadow Glazes, pale green, batch 17, two 2 kg tubs. The job-reference line remains cropped out of this photo.

challenges: Identical supplies do not identify a client commission.
Delayed evidence can resolve one uncertain source to two memberships.
Revising OCR after a correction preserves the corrected membership.
Accounting and creative phases share project identity.
authorNotes: The clients, supplier, venue and order details are invented. The shared supplier receipt is explicitly corrected before its text is revised; its revised text alone is still insufficient for assigning either project.
